node-1.label: Patient presented with right-sided chest pain and dyspnoea for 1 month

node-2.label: Patient was a 66-year-old male, never-smoker, labourer; past history included right-sided pleural effusion 3 years ago treated for 6 months and blunt chest trauma 5 years ago from buffalo impact; no comorbidities, recent instrumentation or surgery.

node-3.label: Chest pain was dull aching, gradually progressive, increased with respiration, and relieved with analgesics; dyspnoea was exertional and gradual in onset, progressively increasing from mMRC grade 1 to 3; no fever, cough, expectoration, or wheeze.

node-4.label: Physical examination: pulse rate 96/min, respiratory rate 25/min, blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, oxygen saturation 96% on room air; respiratory system showed decreased movements in right mammary, infra-axillary, and infrascapular areas, dull percussion note, and decreased breath sounds in affected areas.
